## Xi Jinping in 2024: `2B.5` proxy restraint and responsibility

Best read: **mixed and weak overall.** China’s official line in 2024 still claimed strong nonproliferation controls and diplomatic restraint, but there is also concrete evidence of **PRC-based procurement support for DPRK missile programs**, plus **continued coercive Taiwan operations** and **reluctance to harden pressure on Iran**. I found **no direct 2024 evidence that Xi personally accepted responsibility for foreseeable proxy conduct** or publicly disciplined a proxy/recipient network after it was exposed.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports restraint | [China's Non-Proliferation Policy and Measures](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjlc_665236/fkswt_665240/202406/t20240606_11405135.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-06 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjlc_665236/fkswt_665240/202406/t20240606_11405135.html | China said it does not support, encourage, or assist any country in developing WMD or delivery means, and said it uses export controls and diplomacy to manage proliferation. This is the clearest official nonproliferation baseline. | `2B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.4` |

This supports restraint in official policy terms. | `2B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.4` |

This is anti-escalatory, though still declaratory rather than evidence of enforcement against proxies. | `2B.5`, `1B.4`, `1B.8` |
| Cuts against restraint | [Treasury Targets PRC-based Procurement Network Supporting DPRK Ballistic Missile and Space Programs](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2482) | U.S. Department of the Treasury | 2024-07-24 | https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2482 | Treasury sanctioned a PRC-based network that procured items supporting DPRK ballistic missile and space programs. This is the strongest evidence that Chinese-based actors still enabled destabilizing proliferation despite Beijing’s official nonproliferation line. | `2B.5`, `1B.6` |
| Cuts against restraint | [China voted against IAEA Iran pressure resolution](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zwbd/202412/t20241205_11538812.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-11-22 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zwbd/202412/t20241205_11538812.html | China voted against an IAEA resolution that would have increased pressure on Iran, arguing for diplomacy instead. That is not direct support for destabilization, but it is reluctance to confront a foreseeable proliferation problem by coercive means. | `2B.5`, `1B.6` |
| Cuts against restraint | [PLA conducts joint military drills surrounding Taiwan Island](https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html) | PRC Ministry of National Defense / Xinhua | 2024-05-23 | https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html | Official drills involved combat-readiness patrols, precision strikes, and a “stern warning” to Taiwan independence forces. That is direct destabilizing coercion, not a visible effort to restrain a subordinate force or recipient from escalation. | `2B.5`, `2B.2`, `6A`, `1B.8` |
| Cuts against restraint | [Reuters report on Rocket Force purges](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3270993/chinas-communist-party-targets-another-pla-general-corruption-investigation?UUID=f0bc4b91-7818-4f96-bf67-aa5b46ac9395&next_article_id=3270939&tc=7&tpcc=enlz-globalimpact) | South China Morning Post / Reuters | 2024-07-18 | https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3270993/chinas-communist-party-targets-another-pla-general-corruption-investigation?UUID=f0bc4b91-7818-4f96-bf67-aa5b46ac9395&next_article_id=3270939&tc=7&tpcc=enlz-globalimpact | Reuters reported another senior Rocket Force officer was expelled amid a wider purge of the nuclear-missile force. That points to internal discipline failure, not a demonstrated willingness to accept responsibility for foreseeable proxy or recipient conduct. | `2B.5`, `1B.3`, `1B.7` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for restraint:** China’s 2024 official line strongly endorsed nonproliferation, export control, no-first-use, and diplomatic resolution of Iran and DPRK nuclear issues.
- **Best evidence against restraint:** PRC-based actors still enabled DPRK missile programs, China resisted pressure on Iran, and the Taiwan drills were coercive rather than restrained.
- **Bottom line:** **Xi’s 2024 record is policy-restraining in rhetoric, but weak on enforcement and accountability.** I found **no direct evidence that Xi accepted responsibility for foreseeable proxy conduct** or that he clearly restrained recipients when short-term political interests favored permissiveness.

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence showing:
- Xi publicly acknowledged responsibility for PRC-linked proxy or recipient misconduct,
- Xi ordered punishment of an ally/proxy/client specifically for foreseeable destabilization,
- or a documented Chinese crackdown that clearly traced from a proxy proliferation incident back to top-level accountability.

So the strongest calibrated reading is: **officially anti-proliferation, operationally permissive enough to allow proxy leakage.**
